title: Import torrent files from an opt-in operator-configured inbox
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Simple Torrent has fsnotify import; covrom scans directories every five seconds despite its fsnotify README. Current app has no import inbox. Offer narrow local automation without shell commands or letting watched folders choose arbitrary download destinations.

## Acceptance criteria

- Disabled by default; the trusted operator configures a dedicated inbox outside served downloads and session state. Accept only regular .torrent files through existing bounded metainfo validation, outbound policy and queue admission.
- Handle startup contents, partial writes and atomic rename into the directory. Bound scan/event backlog, file size and concurrent imports; deduplicate repeated events and infohashes across restart.
- Reject symlinks and escapes; no recursive arbitrary filesystem watching or executable hooks. Respect AutoStart and never let an import override the download root or bypass capacity/selection rules.
- Retain source files by default; optional processed/quarantine handling stays confined to the inbox and occurs only after durable acceptance. Retain failed imports with useful visible errors; do not endlessly retry unchanged bad input.
- Test partial/renamed/duplicate/oversized/malformed files, links, a full queue, restart, shutdown/reconfiguration and failed persistence using an isolated directory.

## Sources

- https://github.com/boypt/simple-torrent/blob/6f4942933b71106bae00b4f4c94438e3b315fca2/engine/engineUtil.go#L112-L170
- https://github.com/covrom/cloud-torrent/blob/96fe65ee3121752f31da5e7170b2c18ffda272d7/server/server.go#L143-L194
- https://github.com/covrom/cloud-torrent/blob/96fe65ee3121752f31da5e7170b2c18ffda272d7/server/server.go#L274-L299

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.

## Prerequisites

#76, #78, #74, #73.
